subject: Unscheduled maintenance: safety fix for prefix compaction regression
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@dataforge.io>, DataForge Enterprise Support <support@dataforge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Unscheduled maintenance: safety fix for prefix compaction regression

Hi Tara / DataForge team,

Thanks for the quick signal earlier. We identified a regression in the prefix compaction logic used by our serving runtime that can, under very specific long-tail request patterns, cause KV prefix growth and an elevated memory footprint on older instance families. We are issuing an immediate safety patch to prevent the compaction step from entering the pathological loop.

Planned action (unscheduled, limited window):
- Start: 2026-07-19 19:00 PDT (~1h from now)
- Expected duration: ~3–6 minutes per pod; rolling across the fleet with no more than 1 pod disruption per shard.
- Impact: brief request queuing for affected dedicated nodes (observed < 250ms extra in tests) and automatic failover to warm pool if configured. No customer data will be lost.

What we need from you: none for the immediate fix. If you have pinned instance families or strict single-availability-zone constraints, reply and we'll coordinate a manual window.

Attachments: redwood_prefix_compaction_fix_v1.patch (patch diff), rollback-instructions.txt

I'll send a follow-up once the patch finishes and include a short postmortem. Apologies for the short notice — we pushed this because we've seen increasing risk to tail stability.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com

From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@dataforge.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: DataForge Enterprise Support <support@dataforge.io>
Date: 2026-07-19T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unscheduled maintenance: safety fix for prefix compaction regression

Jonas — thanks for the heads up. We appreciate the proactive approach and the clear high-level impacts. A couple quick Qs for our ops/security team: 

1) Will the change alter any response semantics or token outputs? (we run a strict output validation)
2) If we observe client-side errors during the window, what's the best way to surface them to you?

We are not pinned to a specific instance family; default behavior is fine. Please loop us in if anything changes.

—Tara
Tara Singh
Head of Platform, DataForge
Tara.Singh@dataforge.io

Date: 2026-07-19T18:10:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Unscheduled maintenance: safety fix for prefix compaction regression

Jonas — prepping the rollout now. Quick notes for the deploy steps in case we need to answer customer questions:
- Hotfix is a small compaction-guard change and a metrics toggle. No model weights touched.
- We will enable increased telemetry on the compaction duration histogram so we can quickly detect regressions.
- Post-patch we will run a synthetic smoke across DataForge account endpoints (non-invasive, read-only).

If DataForge sees unexpected outputs, instruct them to capture request IDs (x-rw-request-id) and drop them in this thread. We'll escalate immediately.

Marissa
Director, Production Operations
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@dataforge.io>, DataForge Enterprise Support <support@dataforge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-19T19:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unscheduled maintenance: safety fix for prefix compaction regression

Update: patch applied to the affected Dedicated shard pool serving DataForge at 2026-07-19T19:10 PDT. We observed a ~40ms median extra latency during the compaction handoff in one pod and immediate normalization after placement. No client errors surfaced from our active checks.

We performed the synthetic smoke across DataForge endpoints (read-only) and compared token-level outputs; no semantic changes were observed. That said, if you see anything unexpected, please include the timestamp and x-rw-request-id — we will fast-track a rollback.

Thanks for the rapid coordination. We'll continue monitoring and will post a short incident follow-up with root cause and remediation steps within 12 hours.

Jonas

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Tara Singh <tara.singh@dataforge.io>, DataForge Enterprise Support <support@dataforge.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T02:14:00-07:00
Subject: Post-action update and next steps — prefix compaction safety change (INC-4821)

Tara / DataForge team,

Final update and immediate follow-ups: 

1) What happened: a recent compaction heuristic introduced a corner-case loop that increased prefix-index growth under repeated short-prefix write patterns. This was surfaced by our tail-memory alarms and customer telemetry.
2) Action taken: rolled out redwood_prefix_compaction_fix_v1 across the fleet serving your account at 2026-07-19T19:10 PDT. The patch ensures a cap on compaction iterations per cycle and adds defensive checks to avoid duplicate work.
3) Impact observed: transient latency bump during per-pod handoff (median +40ms, 99th < 320ms in our Canary), no semantic output differences, and memory trend returned to baseline within one compaction window.
4) Verification: we executed a controlled synthetic smoke suite against your endpoints and validated token outputs.

Follow-ups we are committing to: 
- Postmortem document (link below) with timelines, root cause analysis, and a long-term fix plan (INC-4821).
- Backport of the fix to older runtime branches in the next patch cycle.
- Proactive alerting addition: compaction-loop counter and a kill-switch metric (ETA 2 weeks).

Postmortem: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4821
KB/rollback link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-urgent-kb-view

If you have additional questions or want a quick walk-through of the patch, Marissa and I can schedule 30 minutes Thursday. Otherwise, please reply with any request IDs if you noticed anomalies and we will prioritize.

Apologies again for the disruption and thanks for the rapid coordination.

—Jonas
Sr. Incident Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
